description: Grafana read integration, for Grafana Cloud and self-hosted Grafana alike. Actions: list_alerts (alert instances currently firing, pending, silenced, or inhibited, via the Grafana Alertmanager v2 API, filterable by label matcher), list_alert_rules and get_alert_rule (alert rule definitions via the provisioning API), search_dashboards (dashboards and folders by title, tag, and kind), get_dashboard (full dashboard JSON by UID), list_datasources (configured data sources and their UIDs), query_metrics (PromQL expression against a Prometheus-compatible data source over a time range via /api/ds/query). Read-only: the tool performs no creates, updates, or deletes. Authenticates with a Grafana service account token injected by the host as a Bearer header. The tool reads its target hostname from the workspace file `grafana/host`, which must match the host baked into the allowlist below. INSTALL EDIT REQUIRED: replace YOUR_GRAFANA_HOST (2 places: allowlist.host and host_patterns) with your Grafana hostname before installing.

static_token.instructions: Create a Grafana service account with the Viewer role, add a token to it, and store the token. Viewer is sufficient for every action this tool exposes.

auth.instructions:
1. Edit this capabilities file and replace YOUR_GRAFANA_HOST in both places (`allowlist.host` and the credential's `host_patterns`) with your Grafana hostname. Use the bare hostname with no scheme or path, for example `myorg.grafana.net` for Grafana Cloud or `grafana.example.com` for a self-hosted instance. The host allowlist is the security boundary, so it is deliberately pinned to one host per install.
2. In Grafana, go to Administration > Users and access > Service accounts and click Add service account.
3. Give it the Viewer role. Every action in this tool is read-only, so no wider role is needed.
4. Click Add service account token, copy the generated token, and store it on the IronClaw host:

   ```sh
   export GRAFANA_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN=<service account token>
   ```

5. Write the same hostname to the workspace file `grafana/host`. Append a port there if your instance uses one, for example `grafana.example.com:3000`.
6. Run `ironclaw tool install grafana` to register the tool.
7. Self-hosted instances must be reachable over HTTPS with a certificate the IronClaw host trusts.
